findings.title: include_website_name is missing the '?' suffix, so AMS never calls it
findings.body: ActiveModelSerializers filters attributes via methods named `include_<attr>?`. The new method is defined as `def include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never invoked and `website_name` is always serialized — including as `nil` when the user has no website. The intended guard (`website.present?`) has no effect. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: website_name is not declared an untrusted attribute, leaking TL0 users' websites to anonymous viewers
findings.body: The serializer hides `website` from anonymous viewers of TL0 users via `untrusted_attributes :website, ...`, but the newly added `website_name` attribute is not in that list. Since `website_name` is derived directly from `website`, an anonymous visitor can now read a TL0 user's website host (and path) from the `website_name` field even though `website` itself is correctly suppressed. Add `website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (and fix the missing `?` on its include method).

findings.title: website_name returns nil for websites without a scheme or with unparseable URLs
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` returns nil for values like `example.com/user` (no scheme — URI parses it as a path, host is nil) or any malformed URL that survives profile validation, causing `website_name` to be nil and the template's `{{#if model.website_name}}` to hide the website link entirely even though `model.website` is present. Previously the client-side code displayed `website.split('/')[2]`, which also degraded, but the new serializer should fall back to the raw `website` string instead of returning nil so the link remains visible.

findings.title: Query string and fragment are dropped from displayed website name
findings.body: When the domains match, the display value is built as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`, discarding any query string or fragment. A user whose website is `http://example.com/page?id=5` on the same host will see it displayed as `example.com/page`, which no longer represents the actual URL. Include `URI#query`/`fragment` or use `request_uri` when constructing the display path.
